entities.summary: Theodore Pileles Doranites, known as Pileles (Πιλέλης), was a Byzantine Greek aristocrat and military leader in the Empire of Trebizond. Born in an unknown year, he was a prominent member of the Doranites aristocratic family from Trebizond, who played a key role in the civil strife that disrupted the Empire in the 14th century. Pileles was instrumental in several battles, including the Battle of Sarantza in 1337, which was a pivotal moment in the empire's decline. He was succeeded by his son, Theodore II Doranites, who continued his family's legacy in the Empire of Trebizond. Pileles' military prowess and strategic leadership made him a respected figure in the empire, and his legacy continued to shape the region for centuries to come. The fall of Trebizond in 1461 marked the end of an era for Pileles and his family, who had dominated the region for over a century. Despite the empire's decline, Pileles' name remains synonymous with bravery and military excellence in the annals of Byzantine history.
